subject: Transient compute hops, region pinning, and erasure commitments
messages:
From: Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@greenleafhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q on where patient inference runs / cross-border risk

Sean —

Thanks for taking this call yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and legal teams: we need a concise explanation of where inference requests for our production tenant will execute (regions and any third-party hops). Specifically:

- Are there transient compute 'hops' that could route across borders even if we select "US" region?
- Which subprocessors touch request data in the pipeline (both control plane and execution plane)?
- Can you commit to a region-pin in the contract, and if so, what are the exceptions?
- If we issue an erasure request, how quickly is cached/ephemeral state and persistent logs removed?

Can you put together a short evidence packet we can share with our auditors (diagram + short write-up)? We are trying to close procurement next month.

Appreciate it —
Alan
Alan Murphy
Head of Security
GreenLeaf Health

---

(Attachment requested: diagram of hops + list of subprocessors)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where patient inference runs / cross-border risk

Alan —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a short, practical summary below and attached an evidence packet. High-level first, then specifics you can hand to auditors. If you want, we can convert the diagram into a single-page PDF for your SOC review.

1) High-level model of request flow (summary)
- Control plane (API management, auth, audit trails): hosted in the region you choose for your account (we offer US, EU, APAC). These control-plane services may use our platform control plane managed by Redwood in the same region or in a dedicated VPC for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Execution plane (where model inference runs): By default for a "US" tenant we route inference to GPU capacity that is physically located in US regions (e.g., us-west-2, us-east-1). We do not egress inference payloads to other regions under normal operations.
- Transient hops: for hosted customers on multi-tenant pools we may use cross-availability-zone networking within the same cloud region; we do not route inference payloads across country borders for a pinned-region account.

2) Subprocessor summary (who touches the data)
- Execution compute: cloud provider managed GPU instances (we list provider and region in the attached roster).
- Storage/logging: encrypted logs and metrics are stored in the pinned region; long-term analytics exports (if enabled) are sent to S3 buckets you configure.
- Monitoring/observability: traces and alerting metadata are processed by our telemetry pipeline; telemetry is redacted by default and stored in-region for pinned accounts.

3) Region pinning and contractual exceptions
- Region pinning: we can add a region-pinning clause that requires Redwood to keep execution and control-plane processing in the contracted region(s). This covers inference request handling, ephemeral KV caches, and persisted logs.
- Narrow exceptions: emergency failover (regional outage) may trigger cross-region failover to a nearby Redwood region or Dedicated fallback pool; we will only do so after attempts to remediate and will notify customers within our incident SLA. We can require prior approval for any cross-border failover in your contract.

4) Deletion / erasure commitments
- Ephemeral state (KV cache, GPU memory): ephemeral caches are cleared within seconds of session expiry; we treat KV caches as non-persistent and they are not material for long-term retention.
- Short-term traces/metrics: 24–72 hours by default; configurable per-customer.
- Persistent logs / backups: we honor erasure requests and start the deletion workflow within 48 hours; completion for all replicas depends on subprocessor timelines but we typically close everything within 30 days. We will add a clause with SLA-backed timelines if needed.

Attachments included in this reply: redwood-exec-data-sojourns-diagram-v1.pdf (diagram of control plane vs execution plane and subprocessor roster), residency-contract-clause-draft.docx (proposed contract language for region pinning + erasure SLA).

Next steps I propose: 1) I’ll share the simple diagram (attached) for your auditors, 2) Marissa can join to iron out contractual language, 3) we can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive with your security team if they want network traces.

If you want the diagram to highlight particular providers or an on-prem option, tell me which ones and we’ll tailor it.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

From: Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@greenleafhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenleafhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where patient inference runs / cross-border risk

Sean —

Thanks for the quick write-up and attachments — useful. A couple of clarifying points from our legal/IT side:

- Can you confirm that the control plane endpoints (auth, IAM) for a pinned-US tenant will not be routed via EU-based services for authentication or telemetry aggregation? We need an answer we can put directly into the vendor security questionnaire.
- For the emergency failover language: can we require that Redwood attempt to fail over only to US regions and only to EU regions as a last resort, with written consent from GreenLeaf prior to EU failover? Our auditors want a contractual block on automatic cross-border failover.
- For deletion: 30 days is acceptable as long as you can provide a certificate (signed statement) that replicas and backups are included.

Can Marissa or Connor draft the specific sentence(s) we can paste into our vendor review? A short statement for each bullet above is perfect.

Alan

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alan Murphy <alan.murphy@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where patient inference runs / cross-border risk

Alan —

Thanks — below are three short, auditor-ready statements you can paste into your questionnaire or contract redline. Happy to format into a single-paragraph clause if you prefer.

1) Control plane locality: "For accounts contracted with a US region pin, Redwood Inference operates control-plane services (authentication, authorization, audit log collection) within US-based infrastructure; Redwood does not route control-plane authentication traffic through EU-hosted services for such pinned accounts."

2) Emergency failover constraint: "Redwood will attempt automated failover to alternative US regions first. Cross-border failover to EU regions will not occur without prior written consent from the customer, except in cases where a compelled legal process prevents timely notification. Any cross-border failover executed under such compelled circumstances will be logged and reported within the incident timeline specified in Section X of the agreement."

3) Erasure and replica removal: "Upon receipt of a verified erasure request, Redwood will initiate deletion workflows for ephemeral caches, persistent logs, and replicas within 48 hours and use commercially reasonable efforts to complete deletion of all customer data across Redwood-managed and subprocessor systems within 30 calendar days. Redwood will provide a signed attestation of deletion on request."

If you want a single contract-ready paragraph, we can combine these three statements and provide it as a one-line clause. Connor can also prepare a short addendum you can attach to the master services agreement.

Would you like us to add any provider names into the clause or keep it provider-agnostic?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
